lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The Experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Clearwater Sensors appears above the more recent Voltline Robotics role, making the work history harder to scan chronologically.

items.says: Education appears before Experience.
items.because: The recent engineering roles provide more direct evidence of your current professional focus.

items.says: The older Formula Student project takes space from the more current weather-station project and disrupts the résumé’s direction.
items.because: It is older and includes robot-fleet claims that do not fit its stated project.

items.says: The résumé shows no study or work between the degree and the Clearwater Sensors role.
The strongest result in the Clearwater Sensors entry is not the first bullet.
The calibration bullet does not explain what calibration approach the procedure established.
The 60% update-speed improvement does not identify the measure or its baseline.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the percentage measures or assess it without a before-and-after comparison.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the result-and-method phrasing clumsy.
The test-rig bullet reports test volume and frequency but no result from the rig.
items.because: The figure shows how much testing ran, not what the rig accomplished.

items.says: The “which” clause leaves it unclear whether the logger or the saved data helped identify the failures.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The 8 kHz sampling rate has a 4 kHz Nyquist frequency, below the signal’s 5 kHz frequency.

items.says: “So the fault detector could capture it” is wordy and leaves “it” vague.
items.because: The pronoun does not clearly name what the detector captures.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make counter updates atomic or prevent the interrupt handler and main loop from interleaving.

items.says: The claimed race-condition fix has no stated check or result showing that it was resolved.
items.because: Without an observable verification result, the claimed resolution is harder to assess.

items.says: Repeating “counter” makes the sentence unnecessarily redundant.
items.because: The noun appears twice in a short phrase describing the shared variable.

items.says: The opening phrase does not name the firmware change that produced the reported results.
The quantified results are buried at the end of the long bullet.
The promotional description does not identify what the station does or what technical work you performed.
items.because: Its wording gives little evidence of the station’s function, value, or your design or implementation contribution.

items.says: The methods appear before the measurable current reduction.
The sharing bullet does not say what technical contribution made the stations usable or replicable.
The bullet does not identify your specific firmware or testing contribution or its outcome.
items.because: “Worked on” describes involvement without showing what you did or giving a result by which to judge it.

items.says: The robot-fleet motor-controller work pulls the entry away from the stated Formula Student project.
items.because: The entry is about a Formula Student car, but the bullet describes a robot fleet and overlaps with the later employment narrative.

items.says: The dashboard firmware bullet does not say what the firmware enabled or improved.
items.because: The writing and testing process does not show what changed for the dashboard, car, or team.

items.says: The bullet does not say what the tests checked or whether they passed.
The dashboard CAN-bus bullet is not the opening line of the entry.
Passive phrasing obscures your role in writing and testing the firmware.
The robot-fleet bullet’s reduction sizes do not state what they are compared with.
items.because: “Eightfold” and “more than half” give the size of the changes but not the reference values or comparison point.

items.says: The robot-fleet firmware claim appears to duplicate the later Voltline achievement and conflicts with this project’s dates and context.
items.because: Both entries describe a robot fleet and motor-control results, making it unclear which project owns the achievement.
